prompt:
A 1.00 g sample of ammonium nitrate is decomposed in a bomb calorimeter.  The temperature of the calorimeter increases by 6.12 K.  The heat capacity of the system is 1.23 kJ/g ºC.  What is the heat of the reaction in kJ/mole?
Group of answer choices

- 7.53 kJ/mole

-398 kK/mole

- 602 kJ/mole

- 16.1 kJ/mole
judge_reasoning: Candidate [1] applies the calorimetry relation q = CΔT correctly (using the 1.00 g sample with the given heat capacity units) and uses the correct molar mass for NH4NO3, yielding a heat of reaction of about −602 kJ/mol (very close to the expected magnitude/sign). Candidate [2] uses an incorrect molar mass, computes ~497 kJ/mol in the middle, but then commits to −398 kJ/mol despite that mismatch. Candidate [3] and [4] arrive at substantially wrong final values (−16.1 kJ/mol and ~498 kJ/mol respectively) due to major errors in reasoning/handling/sign or molar mass.
